observation: Natural Devanagari Hindi with English terms in brackets. Park-laps analogy covers initialisation, condition and update well. But gives Python code to a Beginner, never addresses the misconception (condition is checked every round, not once), no practice questions.

Switched to Roman Hinglish unasked. Depth suits Intermediate (range step, enumerate, break/continue) but Python-only, so never explains initialisation, condition and update (core key points). No analogy, no misconception, no practice questions. Typo 'kaafireadable'.

Code given to a Beginner. Mirror analogy says reflections go on infinitely, which reinforces the no-base-case misconception. Call stack not explained. Internal slip: says it counts 5 to 1 but code calls countdown(3). Mentions C++/Java but shows only Python. No practice questions.

Thorough on call stack, winding/unwinding, tail recursion and complexity, but overshoots the level (recurrence relations, TCO, DP). Accuracy issues: claims compilers optimise tail calls but example is Python (no TCO); StackOverflowError is Java (Python raises RecursionError); fact() with base case n == 1 never stops for n=0. Never says recursion is not always faster than loops. No analogy, no practice questions.
Best of the five. Devanagari, no code, good ice-tray/egg-tray analogy; covers same type, contiguous memory and index from 0 with an example. Missing fixed size in C and practice questions.
